subject: Materials Science
title: Composites in Civil Engineering
description: A micro-lesson that makes Composites in Civil Engineering usable.

hook.text: A footbridge in Spain has beams of glass-fiber composite — it will never rust or need painting.

buildup.text: Concrete reinforced with FRP bars resists corrosion that destroys steel rebar in bridges.

discovery.text: FRP wraps bonded around old concrete columns restore earthquake resistance without demolition.

twist.text: Composites cost more upfront but last decades longer — real savings come from skipped maintenance.

climax.text: Over 100,000 bridges worldwide now use composite components to extend service life.

punchline.text: Composites don't rust — and that changes infrastructure.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of FRP composites over steel rebar in bridges?
options: FRP is heavier and stronger than steel
FRP resists the corrosion that destroys steel
FRP conducts electricity better than steel
